contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary prose is the more detailed, sourced account (cites published trip reports); timing.totalHrs understates the time.

contradictions.fact: Location, grade and structure of the route's crux

claims.says: The climbing starts up a steep crack/face (crux) for approximately 30 feet of low 5th class, then transitions to Class 4 for about half a rope length
Crux: ~30 ft low 5th class crack/face -- Short technical section, then eases back to 4th class to the top

pitch '4 (Improbable Traverse)', grade '5.8', notes: The route's namesake pitch and best rock; climb ~5.8 moves out right, protected by old fixed pitons. Since a Nov 2021 rockfall, the far end now involves an unprotected 5.9-10- downclimb — verify current condition before committing.

contradictions.why: beta and the itinerary both describe the crux as an easy ~30 ft low-5th-class crack near the START of the climb, but rock_grade (5.8) and pitch_detail place the real crux in the MIDDLE of the route as a distinct 5.8 pitch explicitly named 'Improbable Traverse' -- now effectively 5.9-10- and unprotected since 2021 rockfall damage, information beta/itinerary never mention.
contradictions.internal_resolution: rock_grade + pitch_detail agree on a mid-route 5.8 (now harder) crux; beta/itinerary describe an easier, differently located crux and omit the post-2021 hazard, so a climber relying on beta alone would be unprepared for the real crux.

contradictions.fact: Elevation/location of the route's rock-chimney crux

claims.says: The route is mostly a well-worn boot path with a stretch of Class 2-3 scrambling and one short rock-chimney crux near 5,100 ft.
